subject: Banking
title: Debit Cards vs Credit Cards
description: A quick win: understand Debit Cards vs Credit Cards.

hook.text: Debit pulls money you have. Credit lends money you owe. Same plastic, completely different financial products.

buildup.text: Debit transactions cost merchants about 0.5-1%. Credit costs 1.5-3.5%. The difference is the cost of lending risk.

discovery.text: Credit cards offer stronger fraud protection. Federal law limits your loss to $50. Debit fraud recovery is slower.

twist.text: Banks prefer you use credit because interchange is higher. Reward programs on credit cards exist to steer your choice.

climax.text: The card in your wallet is a business decision by your bank. Every feature nudges you toward higher-fee products.

punchline.text: Same plastic, different economics. Banks prefer credit cards.

quiz.question: Why do banks offer better rewards on credit cards than debit cards?
options: Credit interchange fees are higher, generating more revenue

details.summary: Debit cards withdraw money directly from your bank account at the time of purchase, while credit cards create a short-term loan that you repay later, with each carrying different fee structures, protections, and risks.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing between debit and credit cards affects your fraud protection, spending behavior, credit score, and the fees merchants pay. Understanding the difference helps make smarter financial decisions.
takeaways: Debit transactions pull funds immediately from your checking account
Credit cards offer stronger fraud protection and chargeback rights
Credit cards charge merchants higher interchange fees than debit cards

faq.question: Which card offers better fraud protection?
faq.answer: Credit cards. Federal law limits credit card fraud liability to $50, and most issuers waive even that. Debit card fraud can drain your account before you notice, and recovering funds takes much longer.

faq.question: Why do merchants prefer debit over credit cards?
faq.answer: Debit card interchange fees are significantly lower, often capped at around 0.05 percent plus a fixed fee, versus 1.5 to 3 percent for credit cards. This difference adds up to billions in merchant savings annually.
